name: MKOS Continuous Knowledge Lifecycle
source_attribution: MKOS Continuous Knowledge Lifecycle Specification and the MKOS Constitutional Addendum (roadmap Phase 3.1, owner, 10/24/2026)

change_log.summary: Step 1: lifecycle stages, the eleven mappable concept classes, canonical objectives, the relevance rule table and the exam projection.

Relevance is event driven: dirty flags from the write paths, recompute of only what changed, writes only for rows whose score, band or basis differ; the periodic full sweep is removed (backfill on a rules_version change, read-only audit).
Step 2: lesson and curriculum penetration, lesson enrichment, content layers, the three confidence domains, coverage, gaps; every stage implemented.

doctrine: No knowledge asset may stop at ingestion. Every source passes through every stage below as one workflow. Every stage is deterministic (rules only, no AI).

objectives.id_rule: obj.c.<concept id without its leading 'c.'>: one canonical objective per concept, exam-independent, so any blueprint projects onto the same objective

relevance.note: Deterministic. Score of a knowledge object for a canonical objective = max over paths of (attachment factor of the object to a concept) x (product of hop weights from that concept to the objective's anchor concept), at most max_hops hops. The band is the band value nearest to the score (a tie goes to the lower band). Scores below min_score are pruned. No binary mapping and no small fan-out cap: an object relates to every objective that clears the threshold; max_per_object is a safety ceiling for the per-run budget only, keeping the highest scores. rules_version is stamped on each row as computed_v when the row last changed; bumping it re-backfills the whole graph.

self.why: a concept is foundational to its own canonical objective

attachments.why: an objective or educational object that teaches the concept
an assessment objective on the concept
an educational object or source section covering the concept
evidence supporting knowledge about the concept

via_recommendation.why: a claim, objective or teaching point derived from a recommendation about the concept

dirty.note: Event driven (owner principle: determine once, store the result, update only when reality changes). Write paths mark the changed object in mk_relevance_dirty (kb.js putObject on create, status, type or governance change; graph.js addEdges on hop, attachment and derived_from edges; a canonical objective marks its anchor). The engine expands seeds over the hop radius (concepts: max_hops over the hop relations, any edge status; sources and recommendations: what is derived from them), recomputes concepts, then the objects attached to concepts whose rows changed, and writes only rows whose score, band or basis differ; stale pairs are deleted. There is no periodic sweep. A rules_version change (or a restore, or the first run) marks everything once as a resumable backfill. A rotating read-only audit compares stored rows with the rules every audit_hours and marks any drift.

exam_projection.rule: exam relevance(object, blueprint) = max over the object's objectives of (relevance score x topic weight), topic weight = blueprint objective priority_score / 100, over the blueprint topics that project onto that objective

penetration.rule: For a subject (a changed knowledge object, or a source over its recommendations and what derives from them): objective score = max relevance of the subject's objects to that canonical objective; lesson score = max over the lesson's objectives (canonical objectives of the concepts it teaches, and the objectives its blueprint objective projects onto); curriculum node score = max over the objectives of the concepts it covers; board curriculum (blueprint topic) score = max over the objectives it projects onto; exam score = max over its topics of (objective score x topic priority / 100). Scores below min_score are pruned; at most max_per_kind per kind are kept (a storage ceiling, highest first).
penetration.triggers: Computed from change events only: the relevance dirty queue records every subject whose relevance rows changed (mk_penetration_queue), the lifecycle stage computes it for a source, and impact analysis computes it for the subject of a change event. Never by scanning.

enrichment.rule: A lesson the subject penetrates at min_penetration or more is enhanced instead of regenerated: recommendations on the concepts it teaches created after the lesson was written, the evidence and landmark trials (trial lineage) supporting them, the citation of a guideline family the lesson did not have, and validated clinical pearls created since, each recorded once (mk_enhancements) and listed with the lesson; the asset gets a new minor version (1.4.0 -> 1.5.0) with a content row in mk_asset_store. The asset's basis fingerprint is never touched.
enrichment.absorbs_note: assets.js judge: a lesson whose only reason to regenerate is that more recommendations now cover the topic, or that a new guideline family speaks to it, is enhanced instead. Every other reason (an edition changed or superseded, a recommendation changed, flagged, unvalidated, blueprint weighting, objectives, competencies or relationships changed) still regenerates.

layers.rule: Each knowledge object relevant to a canonical objective falls in one layer, first match: advanced (evidence objects: landmark trials and evidence deep dives; objects whose specialty differs from the objective's; high relevance with low confidence: emerging), core (relevance >= core.min_relevance and confidence >= core.min_confidence, on an exam-relevant objective or any objective when core.allow_unprojected), adjacent (relevance >= adjacent.min_relevance), frontier (the rest down to the relevance threshold). Confidence is the evidence confidence domain when computed, else the object's confidence score / 100.

confidence.note: Three separate domains, 0..1, in mk_confidence. They never change mk_objects.conf or trust.
confidence.precision_note: Scores and factors are rounded to 2 decimals, so the rotating pass rewrites a row only when its rounded value moves.

coverage.knowledge_penetration_pct: 100 x current knowledge objects (recommendations, claims, evidence, educational objects) related at supporting_min or more to an objective that a current shared lesson or a curriculum node reaches / all current knowledge objects. Sent to USAP as knowledge_penetration_pct.
coverage.schedule: Once a day after utc_hour, and again (at most runs_per_day_max runs a day in all) while sources wait at the gaps stage.

rules.when: a canonical objective with no knowledge object at coverage.supporting_min
rules.severity: its highest exam weight (topic priority / 100), or 0.3 off any blueprint

rules.when: a current blueprint objective that projects onto no canonical objective with supporting knowledge
an exam-relevant canonical objective with supporting knowledge and no current shared lesson
a canonical objective with recommendations at supporting_min and no evidence object at coverage.evidence_min
a specialty of the taxonomy whose concept coverage is below specialty_min_pct, or with no current source
a current source past its review date, a current guideline older than stale_years, or a superseded source still cited by a current lesson
a current shared lesson whose lesson confidence is below lesson_confidence_min

gaps.durable_note: Derived: every gap is a deterministic function of objects, edges, blueprints, coverage and confidence, recomputed daily. Owners act by adding or replacing a source in the library, which closes the gap on the next run; no owner state is kept on a gap, so nothing needs mirroring or restoring.

derived.note: A rotating write-on-diff pass over layers and confidence (so recency ages) every pass_hours; changes reach them sooner through the penetration queue and the lifecycle stages.
